raw_response:
I will keep my main land in the usual Quzhou pattern: winter wheat followed by summer maize. That is what fits my fields, my water, and the way people around me farm. I do not want to gamble on a crop I cannot manage easily. Wheat and maize have steady buyers, machine work is easy to hire, and I already understand the timing. I will also keep a small piece for peanuts, because that gives me some cash income and spreads risk if grain price or weather goes against me. On wheat, I will use improved seed, plough the land, return straw, put most fertilizer at sowing and topdress nitrogen once, and irrigate at the key stages instead of watering too often. After wheat harvest, I will plant hybrid summer maize quickly, use less tillage so I do not lose moisture, and keep fertilizer and water tighter because summer rain can help. On peanuts, I will manage them more simply with moderate fertilizer, fewer irrigations, and careful pest watching. I am choosing a steady, familiar, labor-manageable year, not a risky one.
